source.title: The Local Interaction Basis: Identifying Computationally-Relevant and Sparsely Interacting Features in Neural Networks
source.authors: Lucius Bushnaq; S. Heimersheim; Nicholas Goldowsky-Dill; Dan Braun; Jake Mendel; Kaarel Hänni; Avery Griffin; Jörn Stöhler; Magdalena Wache; Marius Hobbhahn

record.tranche_reason: The study trains modular-addition models and reports a grokking-like test-loss change, bearing conceptually on delayed generalization. It does not report the full train/test accuracy trajectory or vary training-set size.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that its modular-addition models grok, but does not give a training-accuracy trajectory at the transition or compare different training-set sizes. Its LIB feature and interaction analyses on modular addition do not track circuit formation over training, so they do not test V2. The CIFAR-10 and language-model analyses do not test for grokking-like delays. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is an interpretability-method paper (LIB versus PCA). The grokked modular-addition transformers serve only as a substrate for analysis. Grokking comes up in one sentence of the training details (Appendix A.1): a sharp test-loss drop after about a third of 60,000 epochs, then 100% train and test accuracy. There is no trajectory, no training-accuracy timing, no data-size sweep and no analysis of the transition. The paper reports only how well its own method performs on already-trained models, so it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The grokking mention is an incidental training detail, not a conclusion. The authors conclude that LIB finds more computationally-relevant and, in some cases, more sparsely interacting features than PCA on toy models (modular addition, CIFAR-10). They also conclude it gives no substantial interpretability or sparsity gains on GPT2-small or TinyStories-1M, and so in its current form does not apply to large language models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a modular-addition decoder-only transformer and reports a grokking-like test-loss change, but uses a fixed 30% training split and does not report a training-set-size sweep or the train-accuracy trajectory around the transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five seeds of grokked modular-addition transformers, LIB features are largely single-frequency Fourier features. The key frequencies are 49, 38 and 36 in the cherry-picked seed. Sparsity and modularity results vary by seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc feature decompositions (LIB versus PCA) of grokked modular-addition models recover Fourier-frequency features, with seed-dependent sparsity and modularity.

record.problems: The grokking report gives no separate seed-level transition results, no train-accuracy trajectory around the test-loss decrease, and no comparison across training-set sizes.

untested.parts: All of it: timing of training-accuracy saturation against the test jump, a chance-to-near-perfect test-accuracy trajectory, and the delay's dependence on training-set size. Only a one-line mention of grokking at a fixed 30% split.
LIB and Fourier features are analysed only on final models, not over training.
Five seeds are analysed for Fourier features, but whether they use the same algorithm is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'limits_scope' label should be dropped. The study does not test grokking, and the missing grokking details are untested parts, not scope limits. AdamW is used with weight decay γ=1 and a 30% split, matching the Nanda et al. recipe, but nothing about weight decay or data size is varied. The CIFAR-10 and language-model analyses do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The timing of training-accuracy saturation relative to the test change, a test-accuracy trajectory from chance, and whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks are not reported.

rows.subject: modular addition model (5 models with different random seeds)
rows.size_stated: 1-layer decoder-only transformer; residual stream width 128; 4 attention heads of width 32; MLP width 512
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular addition modulo 113 using the first 30% of the dataset; the report aggregates the five random-seed models.
rows.measure: Test loss over training and final train/test accuracy
rows.value: The authors report a sharp decrease in test loss after about a third of training; all models achieve 100% accuracy on the train and test sets.
rows.note: One aggregate row: the text reports the temporal test-loss result and final accuracies for the models collectively, without separate seed-level values or a train-accuracy trajectory around the test-loss decrease.
rows.check: This is a training-setup note, not a study result. Appendix A.1 says only that 'grokking', a sharp test-loss decrease, occurs after about a third of training, with 100% final accuracy. It gives no baseline, no training-accuracy saturation time, no test-accuracy trajectory and no data-size variation, so it cannot show V1's delay or its scaling. It should not be scored as a test of V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Five modular-addition models trained with a fixed 30% training split
reader_labels.reason: The report describes a sharp test-loss decrease and eventual 100% train/test accuracy, but does not establish the claimed timing relative to training-accuracy saturation, a chance-to-near-perfect test-accuracy jump, or a delay that grows with smaller datasets (R1).
